chunks: From him, from some of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the expiation for the first part of the month, he said: He should give charity with one dinar; and for the middle part, with half a dinar; and for the last part, with a quarter of a dinar.

I asked: And if he does not have what to expiate with, he said: Let him give charity to one poor person; or else, let him seek forgiveness from Allah and not return [to the act], for indeed seeking forgiveness is repentance and expiation for whoever does not find the means to give any of the expiations.

key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ الطَّمْثِ: Expiation for the first part of the month (or specific act)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for tamth if one cannot afford the financial penalty?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the graduated financial expiation for *al-tamth* (often interpreted as the first emission of semen or a specific ritual impurity), scaling the charity from one dinar to a quarter dinar based on the timing. Crucially, it establishes a theological principle of divine mercy: for those lacking financial means, sincere *istighfar* (seeking forgiveness) serves as a complete substitute for both repentance and expiation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on accessibility in ritual law.
